summary: Someone who sells a ship sells the parts used to sail it, but not the servants or the cargo, unless he says everything in it is sold. Selling a wagon does not include the mules, and selling a yoke does not include the oxen, though Rabbi Yehuda says the price can show what was meant.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a ship
chunks.st: One who sells a ship

chunks.en: has sold the mast and the sail,
chunks.st: has sold along with it the toren, and the nes,

chunks.en: and the anchors,
chunks.st: and the ogin,

chunks.en: and everything used to steer it.
chunks.st: and all of the equipment that is used for directing it.
chunks.basisNote: The names of the ship's parts follow Bartenura.

chunks.he: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הָעֲבָדִים,
chunks.en: But he has not sold the servants who row it,
chunks.st: But he has not sold the slaves who serve as oarsmen,

chunks.en: and not the packing bags,
chunks.st: nor the packing bags that are used for transporting goods,

chunks.en: and not the goods on it.
chunks.st: nor the antikei on the ship.

chunks.en: And when he said to him,
chunks.st: And when one said to the buyer: You are purchasing

chunks.en: It and everything inside it,
chunks.st: it, the ship, and all that it contains,

chunks.en: then all of them are sold.
chunks.st: all of these latter elements are also sold.

chunks.en: If he sold the wagon,
chunks.st: One who sold a wagon [hakkaron]

chunks.en: he has not sold the mules.
chunks.st: has not sold the mules that pull the wagon.

chunks.en: If he sold the mules,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one sold the mules,

chunks.en: he has not sold the wagon.
chunks.st: he has not sold the wagon.

chunks.en: If he sold the yoke,
chunks.st: One who sold a yoke [hatzemed]

words.note: A wooden bar that joins two oxen together for plowing.

chunks.en: he has not sold the oxen.
chunks.st: has not sold the oxen,

chunks.en: If he sold the oxen,
chunks.st: and one who sold the oxen

chunks.en: he has not sold the yoke.
chunks.st: has not sold the yoke.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: The price shows what was sold.
chunks.st: The sum of money indicates what one has sold.

chunks.en: How is that?
chunks.st: How so?

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ מְכוֹר לִי צִמְדְּךָ בְּמָאתַיִם זוּז,
chunks.en: If he said to him, Sell me your yoke for two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: If the buyer said to the seller: Sell me your yoke for two hundred dinars,

words.note: A zuz is a silver coin.

chunks.he: הַדָּבָר יָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין הַצֶּמֶד בְּמָאתַיִם זוּז.
chunks.en: everyone knows that a yoke alone does not cost two hundred zuz.
chunks.explain: So he must have meant the oxen too.
chunks.st: since it is a known matter that a yoke is not sold for two hundred dinars
chunks.stMore: he clearly intended to purchase the oxen as well.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: the price is not a proof.
chunks.st: The sum of money is not proof.

summary: The Rabbis argue whether someone who sells a donkey also sells its saddle and bags. Rabbi Yehuda says it depends on how the buyer asked for it.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a donkey
chunks.st: One who sells a donkey

chunks.en: has not sold its gear.
chunks.st: has not sold its vessels, i.e., its equipment, with it.

chunks.en: Nachum the Mede says,
chunks.st: Naḥum the Mede says:

words.note: A Rabbi of the Mishnah from the land of Madai.

chunks.en: he has sold its gear.
chunks.st: He has sold its vessels.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Sometimes it is sold and sometimes it is not sold.
chunks.st: There are times when the vessels are sold, and there are times when they are not sold.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, הָיָה חֲמוֹר לְפָנָיו וְכֵלָיו עָלָיו,
chunks.en: How is that? If the donkey was in front of him with its gear on it,
chunks.st: How so? If the donkey was before him and its vessels were on it,

chunks.he: וְאָמַר לוֹ מְכוֹר לִי חֲמוֹרְךָ זֶה,
chunks.en: and he said to him, Sell me this donkey of yours,
chunks.st: and the buyer said to him: Sell me this donkey of yours,

chunks.en: then the gear is sold.
chunks.st: its vessels are sold.

chunks.en: But if he asked, Is that donkey yours?
chunks.st: If the buyer said to him: Is the donkey yours; I wish to purchase it,

chunks.en: then the gear is not sold.
chunks.st: its vessels are not sold.

summary: When some things are sold, what comes from them is sold too, like a donkey with its foal or a beehive with its bees, but a cow is sold without her calf. A person who buys what comes out of a dovecote, beehive or olive trees must leave some for the seller.

chunks.en: Someone who sells a mother donkey
chunks.st: One who sells a female donkey

chunks.en: has sold the baby donkey.
chunks.st: has sold its foal along with it.

chunks.en: If he sold the cow,
chunks.st: But one who sold a cow

chunks.en: he has not sold her calf.
chunks.st: has not sold its young.

chunks.en: If he sold a garbage heap,
chunks.st: One who sold a dunghill

chunks.en: he sold its manure.
chunks.st: has sold its manure.

chunks.en: If he sold a pit,
chunks.st: One who sold a cistern

chunks.en: he sold its water.
chunks.st: has sold its water.

chunks.en: If he sold a beehive,
chunks.st: One who sold a beehive

chunks.en: he sold the bees.
chunks.st: has sold the bees in it,

chunks.en: If he sold a dovecote,
chunks.st: and likewise one who sold a dovecote

chunks.en: he sold the doves.
chunks.st: has sold the doves.

chunks.en: Someone who buys the young doves of a dovecote from his friend
chunks.st: One who buys the produce of a dovecote from another,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the doves that will hatch over the course of the year in a dovecote,

chunks.en: lets the first babies fly away for the owner.
chunks.st: must leave [mafriaḥ] the first pair of doves from the brood for the seller.

chunks.en: If he bought the young bees of a beehive,
chunks.st: If one buys the produce of a beehive,
chunks.stMore: i.e., all the bees produced from a beehive over the course of the year,

chunks.en: he takes three swarms, and then they are stopped from making more.
chunks.st: the buyer takes three swarms and then the seller renders the bees impotent,
chunks.stMore: so that they will stop producing offspring and instead produce only honey.

chunks.en: If he bought honeycombs,
chunks.st: One who buys honeycombs

chunks.en: he leaves two combs.
chunks.st: must leave two combs.

chunks.en: If he bought olive trees to cut down,
chunks.st: If one buys olive trees for felling,

chunks.en: he leaves two young shoots.
chunks.st: he must leave two shoots for the seller.

words.note: Small new branches that can grow again.

summary: Someone who buys two trees in another person's field does not get the ground under them, so if they die he has no land. If he buys three trees, he also gets the ground, and keeps it even if the trees die.

chunks.he: הַקּוֹנֶה שְׁנֵי אִילָנוֹת בְּתוֹךְ שְׂדֵה חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: Someone who buys two trees in his friend's field
chunks.st: With regard to one who buys two trees in the field of another,

chunks.en: has not bought the ground.
chunks.st: this one has not acquired any ground, but only the trees.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he has bought the ground.
chunks.st: He has acquired the ground
chunks.stMore: under them. The mishna states a halakha in accordance with the opinion of the first tanna: If the trees

chunks.en: If the trees grew big, the field owner may not cut their branches.
chunks.st: grew, the owner of the field may not cut down
chunks.stMore: their branches, despite the fact that their shade damages his field.

chunks.en: What grows from the trunk is his,
chunks.st: And that which grows out of the trunk is his, i.e., it belongs to the owner of the tree,

chunks.en: and what grows from the roots belongs to the field owner.
chunks.st: but that which grows out of the roots belongs to the owner of the ground.

chunks.en: And if the trees died,
chunks.st: And if the trees died,

chunks.en: he has no ground.
chunks.st: their owner has no rights to the ground where the trees had stood.

chunks.en: If he bought three trees,
chunks.st: If one bought three trees,

chunks.en: he has bought the ground.
chunks.st: he has acquired the ground along with them.

chunks.en: If they grew big, the field owner may cut their branches.
chunks.st: If they grew, the owner of the field may cut down
chunks.stMore: their branches, as he sold a specific piece of land along with the trees, not his entire field.

chunks.he: וְהָעוֹלֶה מִן הַגֶּזַע וּמִן הַשָּׁרָשִׁין, שֶׁלּוֹ.
chunks.en: What grows from the trunk and from the roots is his.
chunks.st: And that which grows out of the trunk and out of the roots is his, i.e., it belongs to the owner of the trees.

chunks.en: And if the trees died,
chunks.st: And if the trees died,

chunks.en: he still has the ground.
chunks.st: the owner of the trees still has possession of the ground, as it was sold along with the trees.

summary: When someone sells parts of a large animal, like a cow, each part is sold on its own. With a small animal, like a sheep, selling the head includes the legs, and selling the windpipe includes the liver.

chunks.en: Someone who sells the head of a large animal
chunks.st: One who sells the head of a large domesticated animal

chunks.en: has not sold the legs.
chunks.st: has not sold along with it the forelegs,
chunks.stMore: as each part is considered important in its own right.

chunks.en: If he sold the legs,
chunks.st: All the more so, if one sold the forelegs

chunks.en: he has not sold the head.
chunks.st: he has not sold the head.

chunks.en: If he sold the windpipe and lungs,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one sold the windpipe and the lungs

chunks.en: he has not sold the liver.
chunks.st: he has not sold the liver,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that they are sometimes attached,

chunks.en: If he sold the liver,
chunks.st: and if he sold the liver

chunks.en: he has not sold the windpipe.
chunks.st: he has not sold the windpipe and lungs.

chunks.en: But with a small animal:
chunks.st: But in the case of small domesticated animals,

chunks.en: if he sold the head,
chunks.st: if one sold the head

chunks.en: he has sold the legs.
chunks.st: he has sold the forelegs,

chunks.en: If he sold the legs,
chunks.st: although if one sold the legs

chunks.en: he has not sold the head.
chunks.st: he has not sold the head.

chunks.en: If he sold the windpipe,
chunks.st: Likewise, if one sold the windpipe and lungs

chunks.en: he has sold the liver.
chunks.st: he has sold the liver,

chunks.en: If he sold the liver,
chunks.st: but if he sold the liver

chunks.en: he has not sold the windpipe.
chunks.st: he has not sold the windpipe and lungs.

summary: If a seller promised good wheat and it turned out bad, the buyer may cancel the sale, and if he said bad and it was good, the seller may cancel. If what was given was a different thing from what was promised, like vinegar instead of wine, either one may cancel.

chunks.en: There are four rules about sellers.
chunks.st: There are four basic cases with regard to sellers and buyers.

chunks.he: מָכַר לוֹ חִטִּים יָפוֹת וְנִמְצְאוּ רָעוֹת,
chunks.en: If he sold him wheat as good, and it was found to be bad,
chunks.st: If the seller sold him wheat and said that the wheat was good, and it is found to be bad,

chunks.en: the buyer can back out.
chunks.st: the buyer, but not the seller, can renege on the sale.

chunks.en: If he said bad, and it was found to be good,
chunks.st: If the seller sold him what he thought was bad wheat and it is found to be good,

chunks.en: the seller can back out.
chunks.st: the seller can renege on the sale but the buyer cannot.

chunks.en: If bad, and it was found to be bad,
chunks.st: If he sold bad wheat and it is found to be bad,

chunks.en: or good, and it was found to be good,
chunks.st: or good wheat and it is found to be good,

chunks.he: אֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם יָכוֹל לַחֲזֹר בּוֹ.
chunks.en: neither of them can back out.
chunks.st: neither one of them can renege on
chunks.stMore: the sale, as the condition of the sale was met.

chunks.en: If he sold dark wheat, and it was found to be white,
chunks.st: If the seller sold reddish-brown wheat and it is found to be white,

chunks.en: or white, and it was found to be dark,
chunks.st: or white wheat and it is found to be reddish-brown,

chunks.he: עֵצִים שֶׁל זַיִת וְנִמְצְאוּ שֶׁל שִׁקְמָה,
chunks.en: olive wood, and it was found to be sycamore wood,
chunks.st: and similarly, if he sold olive wood and it is found to be wood of a sycamore,

chunks.en: or sycamore, and it was found to be olive,
chunks.st: or he sold wood of a sycamore and it is found to be wood of an olive tree,

chunks.en: wine, and it was found to be vinegar,
chunks.st: or if the seller sold him wine and it is found to be vinegar,

chunks.en: or vinegar, and it was found to be wine,
chunks.st: or vinegar and it is found to be wine,

chunks.en: both of them can back out.
chunks.st: in all of these cases both the seller and the buyer can renege on
chunks.stMore: the sale. Since the sale was for a different item than that which was delivered, the transaction can be nullified even if there was no mistake with regard to the price.

summary: When someone buys produce, he owns it once he pulls it to himself, even if it was not measured yet; measuring alone is not enough. Flax is bought only when the buyer lifts it and carries it, and flax still growing is bought when he picks some of it.
stIntro: This mishna discusses several methods of acquiring movable property. With regard to

chunks.en: Someone who sells produce to his friend:
chunks.st: one who sells produce to another,

chunks.en: if the buyer pulled it but did not measure it, he has bought it.
chunks.st: if the buyer pulled the produce but did not measure it, he has acquired
chunks.stMore: the produce through the act of acquisition of pulling.

chunks.en: If he measured it but did not pull it, he has not bought it.
chunks.st: If he measured the produce but did not pull it, he has not acquired
chunks.stMore: it, and either the seller or the buyer can decide to rescind the sale.

chunks.en: If he is smart,
chunks.st: If the buyer is perspicacious
chunks.stMore: and wants to acquire the produce without having to pull it, and he wishes to do so before the seller could change his mind and decide not to sell,

chunks.en: he rents the place where it is.
chunks.explain: Then his own place makes it his right away.
chunks.st: he rents its place,
chunks.stMore: where the produce is located, and his property immediately effects acquisition of the produce on his behalf.

chunks.en: Someone who buys flax from his friend
chunks.st: With regard to one who buys flax from another,

words.note: A plant used to make linen cloth.

chunks.en: has not bought it
chunks.st: because flax is usually carried around this purchaser has not acquired it

chunks.en: until he carries it from place to place.
chunks.st: until he carries it from place to place
chunks.stMore: and acquires it by means of the act of acquisition of lifting. Pulling the flax is ineffective.

chunks.en: And if it was still growing in the ground,
chunks.st: And if it was attached to the ground,

chunks.en: and he picked any amount, he has bought it.
chunks.st: and he detached any amount, he has acquired it, as the Gemara will explain.

summary: If the price of wine or oil changes during a sale, it depends on whether the measuring cup was already full. A seller must let three extra drops drip into the buyer's jug, but a busy storekeeper does not have to.

chunks.en: Someone who sells wine and oil to his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells food or drink that has an established price, such as wine and oil, to another,

chunks.en: and the price went up or down:
chunks.st: and the price rises or falls
chunks.stMore: and the buyer or the seller wishes to renege on the sale,

chunks.he: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַלְּאָה הַמִּדָּה, לַמּוֹכֵר.
chunks.en: if it was before the measuring cup was filled, it is the seller's.
chunks.st: if the price changed before the measuring vessel is filled, the merchandise still belongs to the seller and he can cancel the sale.

chunks.en: Once the measuring cup was filled, it is the buyer's.
chunks.st: Once the measuring vessel is filled the merchandise belongs to the buyer, and the seller can no longer cancel the sale.

chunks.en: And if there was a middleman between them,
chunks.st: And if there was a middleman [sarsur] between them

words.note: A person who helps make a sale between a buyer and a seller.

chunks.en: and the barrel broke,
chunks.st: and the barrel belonging to the middleman, being used to measure the merchandise, broke
chunks.stMore: during the transaction and the merchandise is ruined,

chunks.en: it broke for the middleman.
chunks.explain: The middleman pays for the loss.
chunks.st: it broke for the middleman,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he is responsible for the ruined merchandise. The mishna teaches an additional halakha with regard to sales:

chunks.en: And the seller must let three drops drip for him.
chunks.st: And anyone who sells wine, oil, or similar liquids is obligated, after he transfers the liquid into the buyer’s vessel, to drip for him three extra drops from the measure.

chunks.en: If he tipped it and squeezed out the rest,
chunks.st: After he drips those three drops, if he turned the barrel on its side and drained
chunks.stMore: out the last bits of liquid that it contained,

chunks.en: that belongs to the seller.
chunks.st: this belongs to the seller
chunks.stMore: and he is not required to give these last drops to the buyer.

chunks.he: וְהַחֶנְוָנִי אֵינוֹ חַיָּב לְהַטִּיף שָׁלֹשׁ טִפִּין.
chunks.en: And a storekeeper does not have to let three drops drip.
chunks.st: And a storekeeper is not obligated to drip three drops, because he is too busy to do this constantly.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: On Erev Shabbos as it gets dark, he does not have to.
chunks.st: If the sale occurs on Shabbat eve as nightfall arrives, one is exempt
chunks.stMore: from dripping these three drops, as there is a need to complete the transaction before Shabbat begins.

summary: A father sent his small son to a store with a coin, and the storekeeper gave the boy oil and change, but the boy broke the jug and lost the coin. The Sages say the storekeeper must pay, but Rabbi Yehuda says he does not, since the father sent the boy for this.

chunks.en: Someone who sends his son to a storekeeper
chunks.st: With regard to one who sends his son to a storekeeper

chunks.en: with a coin in his hand,
chunks.st: with a pundeyon, a coin worth two issar, in his hand,

chunks.en: and he measured out oil for an issar
chunks.st: and the storekeeper measured oil for him for one issar

chunks.en: and gave him the other issar back,
chunks.st: and gave him the second issar as change,

chunks.he: שָׁבַר אֶת הַצְּלוֹחִית וְאִבֵּד אֶת הָאִסָּר,
chunks.en: and the boy broke the jug and lost the issar:
chunks.st: and the son broke the jug and lost the issar,

chunks.en: the storekeeper must pay.
chunks.explain: He should not have given them to a small child.
chunks.st: the storekeeper
chunks.stMore: must compensate the father, as he gave the jug and coin to one who is not halakhically competent.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says he does not have to pay,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda exempts him from liability,

chunks.en: because that is why the father sent him.
chunks.st: as he holds that the father sent his son in order to do this, i.e., to bring back the jug and coin.

chunks.en: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
chunks.st: And the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda with regard to a case

chunks.en: when the jug was in the child's hand
chunks.st: when the jug is in the hand of the child

chunks.en: and the storekeeper poured the oil into it,
chunks.st: and the storekeeper measured the oil into it

chunks.en: that the storekeeper does not have to pay.
chunks.st: that the storekeeper is exempt if the child breaks the jug.

summary: Sellers must clean their measuring cups and weights so that nothing sticks to them and the buyer gets less. The mishnah says how often a big seller, a homeowner and a storekeeper must clean them.

chunks.he: הַסִּיטוֹן מְקַנֵּחַ מִדּוֹתָיו אַחַת לִשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: A big seller cleans his measuring cups once every thirty days,
chunks.explain: Leftover wine or oil sticks inside and makes the cup hold less.
chunks.st: A wholesaler [hassiton] must clean his measuring vessels, which are used for measuring liquids such as oil and wine, once every thirty days,
chunks.stMore: because the residue of the liquids sticks to the measure and reduces its capacity.

words.note: A person who sells large amounts.

chunks.he: וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת אַחַת לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: and a homeowner once every twelve months.
chunks.st: And a homeowner who sells his goods must clean his measuring vessels only once every twelve months.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It is the other way around.
chunks.st: The matters are reversed.
chunks.stMore: In the case of one who is constantly using his vessels for selling merchandise the residue does not adhere to the measuring vessel, and therefore a wholesaler must clean his measures only once a year. But in the case of a homeowner, who does not sell as often, the residue adheres to the measuring vessel; therefore, he must clean them every thirty days.

chunks.en: A storekeeper cleans his measuring cups twice a week,
chunks.st: A storekeeper, who constantly sells merchandise in small quantities, cleans his measuring vessels twice a week

chunks.en: and wipes his weights once a week,
chunks.st: and cleans his weights once a week;

chunks.he: וּמְקַנֵּחַ מֹאזְנַיִם עַל כָּל מִשְׁקָל וּמִשְׁקָל:
chunks.en: and cleans the scale after every weighing.
chunks.st: and he cleans the pans of his scales after each and every weighing,
chunks.stMore: to ensure that no merchandise has adhered to the pans, thereby increasing their weight.

summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says only cups used for liquids need cleaning. A seller must give a little extra when he weighs, and he must measure the way people do in that place.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: When is this said? With wet things.
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, that it is necessary to clean a measuring vessel, said? With regard to moist
chunks.stMore: items, which are likely to adhere to the measuring vessels.

chunks.en: But with dry things, he does not need to.
chunks.st: But with regard to dry goods, which do not adhere to the measuring vessels, one does not need to clean his measuring vessels.

chunks.en: And he must let the scale tip down a tefach for the buyer.
chunks.st: And before adding the weights and merchandise the seller is obligated to let the pans of the scale that will hold the merchandise tilt an extra handbreadth for the buyer by adding a weight to that side.

chunks.en: If he weighed it exactly even,
chunks.st: If the seller weighed for him exactly,
chunks.stMore: i.e., with the scales equally balanced initially, instead of allowing the scales to tilt an extra handbreadth,

chunks.en: he gives him extra:
chunks.st: he must give the buyer additional amounts [geirumin],

chunks.he: אֶחָד לַעֲשָׂרָה בַּלַּח וְאֶחָד לְעֶשְׂרִים בַּיָּבֵשׁ.
chunks.en: one tenth with wet things, and one twentieth with dry things.
chunks.st: an additional one-tenth in the case of liquids sold by weight, and an additional one-twentieth in the case of dry
chunks.stMore: goods. The mishna continues to discuss the correct method of weighing: In

chunks.en: In a place where people measure with small cups,
chunks.st: a place where they were accustomed to measure merchandise in several stages with a small measuring vessel,

chunks.en: he may not measure with a big one.
chunks.st: one may not measure all the items at once with a single large measuring vessel.

chunks.en: With a big one, he may not measure with small ones.
chunks.st: In a place where they measure with one large measuring vessel, one may not measure with several small measuring vessels.

chunks.en: Where they level it off, he may not heap it up.
chunks.st: In a place where the custom is to level the top of the measuring vessel to remove substances heaped above its edges, one may not heap it,

chunks.en: Where they heap it up, he may not level it off.
chunks.st: and where the custom is to heap it, one may not level it.
